levelIntroduction.title: Welcome to Conditional Castle! 🤔
levelIntroduction.description: Conditionals are like making choices! Just like 'IF it's raining, THEN bring an umbrella.' In code, conditionals help the computer make decisions based on what's true or false.

concepts.name: What is a Conditional?
concepts.explanation: A conditional checks if something is true or false, then decides what to do. It's like asking a question before taking action!

concepts.name: IF and ELSE
concepts.explanation: IF means 'do this when true'. ELSE means 'do this when false'. Together they help make smart decisions.

concepts.name: Comparison Operators
concepts.explanation: We use symbols like === (equals), > (greater than), < (less than) to compare things and make decisions.

levelIntroduction.readyMessage: Ready to help our ghost make the right choices? Let's go!

challenges.title: The Backwards Door
challenges.description: The ghost can't get through the door! Fix it so it outputs: Door opens!
challenges.tip: Think about when the door should open - when you have a key or when you don't? Make sure your condition matches that logic!

validationRules.name: has-if-statement
validationRules.description: Code must contain conditional logic (if statement)
validationRules.feedbackMessage: The if statement is missing! You need to keep the original conditional logic and fix the condition to check when hasKey is true.

validationRules.name: has-hasKey-check
validationRules.feedbackMessage: You need to check the hasKey variable! The door should open when hasKey is true, not false.

validationRules.name: no-direct-console-cheat
validationRules.description: Code must contain the original logic structure
validationRules.feedbackMessage: You can't just write the answer directly! Keep the original code with the hasKey variable and if statement, then fix the condition.

hints: The door should open when hasKey is true, but the condition checks for false!
Look at the if statement - it says 'if hasKey === false', but we want it to be true!
Change 'false' to 'true', or just write 'if (hasKey)' which means the same thing!
challenges.educationalContent: Conditionals let us make decisions in code. 'if (condition)' means 'do this when the condition is true'. We can check if something equals true, or just write the variable name if it's already true or false!

challenges.title: The Wrong Comparison
challenges.description: The ghost needs at least 50 energy to haunt. Fix it so it outputs: Ready to haunt!
challenges.tip: Think about what 'at least 50' means - does it include 50 itself or only numbers higher than 50?

validationRules.name: greater-than-or-equal
validationRules.feedbackMessage: You need to use >= instead of > to include energy that's exactly 50. 'At least 50' means 50 or more!

validationRules.name: has-if-statement
validationRules.feedbackMessage: The if statement is missing! Keep the original code structure and just fix the comparison operator.

validationRules.name: has-energy-variable
validationRules.feedbackMessage: You need to check the energy variable! Don't just hardcode the output.

hints: The ghost needs AT LEAST 50 energy, which means 50 or more!
The symbol '>' means 'greater than', so it doesn't include 50 itself!
Change '>' to '>=' which means 'greater than or equal to' - that includes 50!
challenges.educationalContent: Comparison operators help us compare numbers: '>' means greater than, '<' means less than, '>=' means greater than or equal to, and '<=' means less than or equal to. Choose the right one for what you need!

challenges.title: The Missing Else
challenges.description: The ghost wants to say 'Too cold!' when temperature is below 60. Fix it so it outputs: Too cold!
challenges.tip: What should happen when the temperature is below 60? You need to handle both cases - when it's warm enough and when it's not!

validationRules.name: has-if-statement
validationRules.feedbackMessage: The if statement is missing! Keep the original conditional logic.

validationRules.name: has-else
validationRules.feedbackMessage: You need to add an else block to handle when temperature is below 60!

validationRules.name: has-temperature-check
validationRules.feedbackMessage: You need to check the temperature variable! Don't just hardcode the output.

hints: When temperature is less than 60, nothing happens! We need an 'else' part.
The 'else' block runs when the 'if' condition is false.
Add 'else { console.log('Too cold!'); }' after the closing brace!
challenges.educationalContent: The 'else' part of a conditional runs when the 'if' condition is false. It's like saying 'if this is true, do this, otherwise do that'. Not every if needs an else, but it's useful when you want something to happen either way!

challenges.title: The Confused Logic
challenges.description: The ghost wants to haunt only when it's nighttime AND the moon is full. Fix it so it outputs: Perfect time to haunt!
challenges.tip: The ghost needs BOTH conditions to be true for perfect haunting. Think about which logical operator requires both things to be true!

validationRules.name: logical-and
validationRules.feedbackMessage: You need to use && (AND) instead of || (OR). The ghost needs BOTH nighttime AND full moon to haunt perfectly!

validationRules.name: has-if-statement
validationRules.feedbackMessage: The if statement is missing! Keep the original code structure.

validationRules.name: checks-both-conditions
validationRules.description: Code must check both isNighttime and isFullMoon
validationRules.feedbackMessage: You need to check both isNighttime and isFullMoon variables!

hints: The ghost needs BOTH nighttime AND full moon, not just one or the other!
The symbol '||' means 'or' - it's true if either condition is true.
Change '||' to '&&' which means 'and' - both conditions must be true!
challenges.educationalContent: Logical operators combine conditions: '&&' means AND (both must be true), '||' means OR (at least one must be true), and '!' means NOT (flips true to false or false to true). Choose the right operator for your logic!

challenges.title: The Inverted Check
challenges.description: The ghost wants to haunt when the door is NOT locked. Fix it so it outputs: Ghost enters the room!
challenges.tip: The ghost should enter when the door is NOT locked. Think about how to check for the opposite of a condition!

validationRules.name: has-not-operator
validationRules.feedbackMessage: You need to use the ! (NOT) operator before isDoorLocked. The ghost should enter when the door is NOT locked!

validationRules.name: has-if-statement
validationRules.feedbackMessage: The if statement is missing! Keep the original code structure.

validationRules.name: checks-door-locked
validationRules.feedbackMessage: You need to check the isDoorLocked variable!

hints: The ghost should enter when the door is NOT locked!
Right now it checks if the door IS locked, which is backwards.
Add a '!' before isDoorLocked to flip it: '!isDoorLocked' means 'not locked'!
challenges.educationalContent: The '!' operator means NOT - it flips true to false and false to true. So '!isDoorLocked' means 'the door is not locked'. It's a quick way to check for the opposite of something!

challenges.title: The Age Check
challenges.description: The ghost needs to check if someone is old enough (13 or older) to enter. Fix it so it outputs: Welcome to the haunted house!
challenges.tip: Someone who is exactly 13 should be old enough to enter. Does your condition include 13 or only ages above 13?

validationRules.name: greater-than-or-equal
validationRules.feedbackMessage: You need to use >= instead of > to include people who are exactly 13. '13 or older' means 13 is included!

validationRules.name: has-if-statement
validationRules.feedbackMessage: The if statement is missing! Keep the original code structure.

validationRules.name: checks-age
validationRules.feedbackMessage: You need to check the age variable! Don't just hardcode the output.

hints: Someone who is exactly 13 should be allowed in!
'age > 13' means older than 13, but not 13 itself.
Change '>' to '>=' to include 13-year-olds!
challenges.educationalContent: When checking ages or limits, think carefully: do you want to include the number itself? Use >= or <= to include it, or > and < to exclude it.

challenges.title: The Else If Chain
challenges.description: The ghost wants different messages for different scare levels. Fix it so it outputs: Pretty spooky!
challenges.tip: A scare level of 50 should be considered 'Pretty spooky!' Make sure your condition includes the boundary number!

validationRules.name: has-greater-than-or-equal
validationRules.description: Must use >= in the else if condition
validationRules.feedbackMessage: You need to change > to >= in the 'else if' condition to include scare level 50!

validationRules.name: has-if-statement
validationRules.feedbackMessage: The if statement is missing! Keep the original code structure.

validationRules.name: has-else-if
validationRules.description: Code must have else if structure
validationRules.feedbackMessage: The else if chain is missing! Keep the original code structure.

validationRules.name: checks-scare-level
validationRules.feedbackMessage: You need to check the scareLevel variable!

hints: A scare level of exactly 50 should be 'Pretty spooky!'
The condition 'scareLevel > 50' doesn't include 50 itself.
Change '>' to '>=' to include 50 in the 'Pretty spooky' range!
challenges.educationalContent: Else if chains let us check multiple conditions in order. The first true condition wins! Make sure your ranges don't have gaps or overlaps.
